NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. Regular Orange County Great Park Board meetings are broadcast live every 4th Tuesday of the month at 2 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 2 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live Orange County Great Park meeting), Wednesdays at 8 a.m., Thursdays at 7 p.m., and Saturdays at 7 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live Orange County Great Park meeting) until the next Orange County Great Park Board meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council/Successor Agency meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv. For more information, please contact the Clerk of the Board/City Clerk's office at (949) 724-6205.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk/Clerk of the Board and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council/Great Park Board meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org and the Orange County Great Park website at ocgp.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council/Orange County Great Park Board meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk/Clerk of the Board staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council/Successor Agency/Orange County Great Park Board regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk/Clerk of the Board's Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk/Clerk of the Board staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk’s Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us. Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City's system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk/Clerk of the Board's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL

  June 22, 2021
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER

The regular joint meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:11 p.m. on
June 22, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza,
Irvine, California; Mayor/Chairwoman Khan presiding.

ROLL CALL

  Present: 5 Councilmember/Boardmember  Larry Agran
  Councilmember/Boardmember  Mike Carroll
  Councilmember/Boardmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor/Vice Chairwoman  Tammy Kim
  Mayor/Chairwoman  Farrah N. Khan

Chairwoman Khan announced that City Hall was now open to the public, allowing
members of the public to physically attend and participate in Great Park Board meetings,
and noted the current guidelines for face coverings. She also noted that 1) the meeting
was broadcast live on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse
Channel 99, and livestreamed online at cityofirvine.org; 2) members of the public would
continue to have the ability to provide live comments on agenda items via Zoom; and 3)
the City of Irvine continued to sanitize surfaces and equipment in the Council Chamber
and throughout City Hall.

In addition, Carl Petersen, Secretary / Clerk of the Board, provided instructions on how to
participate in the meeting; and noted that the e-comment feature had been extended,
which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments on all agenda
items, which would be included as part of the official record and uploaded to the City’s
website.
 City Council Minutes  June 22, 2021

  Mayor Khan also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items
  not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor Khan introduced Boy Scout Troop 2279, who led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Malti Maheta, founding member from Indian Community of Irvine, provided the invocation.

  1.  PRESENTATIONS

  1.1  Enforcement Efforts by Irvine Police Department on Loud Exhaust
  and Racing Vehicles

  This presentation was agendized at the request of Councilmembers
  Agran and Kuo, who noted concerns expressed by residents related to
  loud exhaust and racing vehicles and the importance of addressing those
  concerns.

  Jasper Kim and Garrett Gales, Police Sergeants, provided a brief update
  on enforcement efforts by the Irvine Police Department.

  City Council discussion included: questioning whether those arrested
  were primarily residents or residents of other cities; inquired about
  whether new enforcement efforts were effective; questioned fiscal
  impacts associated with street racing; noted certain locations of areas
  needing enforcement; questioned whether loud exhaust equipment was
  an aftermarket issue or if stock automobiles were also contributing
  factors; inquired about whether closed circuit television (CCTV) cameras
  assisted with enforcement efforts; questioned available resources and
  whether any additional ones were needed to assist with enforcement
  efforts; questioned the inspection process for modified vehicles; and
  inquired about whether air support was used for enforcement efforts.

  Mike Hamel, Director of Public Safety/Chief of Police, noted that
  enforcement efforts are concentrated on specific areas when identified..

  Justin Fong, Irvine resident, expressed concern related to certain road
  designs.

  Gil Nelsen, Irvine resident, suggested grant funds be used toward
  technology to assist with enforcement efforts.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  June 22, 2021

  Steve L, Irvine resident, noted his support for public safety, and
  expressed concerns related to street racing and lack of enforcement on
  some City streets.

  1.2  Municipal Broadband Assessment Study

  This presentation was agendized at the request of Mayor Khan and Vice
  Mayor Kim.

  Nick Rycroft, Technology Program Manager, provided an overview of the
  assessment study and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: noting consistent concerns expressed
  by resident with respect to reliable broadband service and the importance
  of providing such service; suggested internet services be made part of
  the City’s infrastructure; explore revenue opportunities related to
  providing/leasing broadband services; and questioned next steps.

  Kristen Camuglia, Cox Communications representative, noted that the
  company was looking forward to working with staff and consultants
  during the assessment study process.

  Jose Cantañeda suggested that staff and consultants work
  collaboratively, and noted the importance of Councilmembers’
  involvement and community input with respect to broadband service in
  the City.

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Mayor Khan made the following announcements:

  •  A Virtual Town Hall meeting, hosted by Waste Management, will be held on
  Wednesday, June 23 from 9:30 to 10:30 a.m. to discuss residential service and
  COVID-19 staffing. Waste Management will also provide information about
  updating online account communication preferences and how to contact their
  Customer Service. Waste Management representatives will be available for
  questions following the presentation. No registration is required. For information
  on how to participate in the meeting, visit cityofirvine.org.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  June 22, 2021

  •  Mayors are taking part in the U.S. Conference of Mayors Challenge to get 70% of
  adults vaccinated with at least one shot before July 4. Irvine can take it even
  further, and has set a goal of having 75% of eligible Irvine residents fully vaccinated
  by the Fourth of July. The City was well in the way to reaching that goal, with 69%
  of eligible Irvine residents fully vaccinated and 78% having received at least one
  dose. Vaccines are one of the most powerful tools to end the COVID-19 pandemic
  and keep the community safe. There are several opportunities for vaccinations,
  which include a vaccination event at Diamond Jamboree Shopping Center on
  Wednesday, July 15 and Sunday, July 18 from 9 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Appointments
  can be made at yourirvine.org. The Orange County Great Park drive-thru
  vaccination clinic is also available on Wednesday, July 15 and Friday, July 23, from
  8 to 11 a.m. To learn more, visit cityofirvine.org/vaccine. As the City focuses on
  bringing additional vaccination clinics to local neighborhoods, the Great Park site
  will transition to a more convenient and accessible mobile unit in early July. For a
  list of all vaccination sites in Irvine, visit the City’s website at
  cityofirvine.org/covid19 and click on COVID-19 Vaccine Resources.

  •  The City had been recognized for excellence in financial reporting for the 42nd
  consecutive year. The Government Finance Officers Association presented the
  City with a Certificate of Achievement for Excellence in Financial Reporting for the
  Comprehensive Annual Financial Report, which summarizes financial activity for
  the previous fiscal year. The award is the highest form of recognition in
  governmental accounting and financial reporting, and represents a significant
  accomplishment by staff in the Financial Management & Strategic Planning
  Department. The Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) is available via
  the City’s website at cityofirvine.org/transparency by clicking Financial Reports.

  •  Community members are invited to attend the Joint Irvine Police Department and
  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Open House on Sunday, June 27 from 1
  p.m. to 5 p.m. at the Orange County Great Park. OCFA’s equipment display will
  include a fire engine, fire truck, hazardous material truck, and the Jaws of Life
  rescue equipment. Irvine Police will also have an interactive display, including a
  Police K-9, horses from the Mounted Unit, drones, a photo booth with police
  equipment, and a swat rescue vehicle. To register, visit cityofirvine.org and click
  June 27 on the City’s calendar.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Agran to adopt the following
  provisions in the form of a City Council resolution:

  1) Reaffirm the selection of the City-owned, 125-acre ARDA site as the
  only available location in the City of Irvine for the development of the
  Southern California Veterans Memorial Park & Cemetery
  2) Actively and aggressively pursue development of the Southern
  California Veterans Memorial Park & Cemetery at the ARDA site
  3) Not pursue or permit the development of the Southern California
  Veterans Memorial Park & Cemetery at any other location within the
  City of Irvine; and
  4) Not sell, lease, or otherwise convey any property within the City of
  Irvine, other than the ARDA site, for development or use as the
  Southern California Veterans Memorial Park & Cemetery.
  5) Direct the City Manager to return to the City Council within 30 days
  with:
  a. Demolition, cleanup and site clearance plan for the ARDA site,
  including a start-date for on-site demolition to commence on or
  before September 1, 2021
  b. Request for Proposals for conceptual plans for the following
  features of the Veterans Memorial Park:
  i. the approximately 25-acre perimeter park surrounding the
  Veterans Cemetery and the entire ARDA site, comprised of
  large berms, trees, trails, memorial/botanical gardens, and
  other appropriate memorial installations;
  ii. the restoration and repurposing of the historic on-site aircraft
  control tower and airplane hangars as an aviation museum;
  and
  iii. the forestation of the approximately 35 acres of the ARDA
  site bounded by Cadence, Pusan Way and Irvine Boulevard.
  6) The City-incurred costs to implement the demolition, cleanup and site
  clearance plan for the ARDA site, estimated at $5 million, shall be
  paid from the City’s Great Park Development Funds — to be
  reimbursed by the State and/or the Federal Government as part of the
  negotiated ARDA site acquisition and transfer agreements that will
  establish the state-owned, state-funded Southern California Veterans
  Memorial Park & Cemetery, anticipated to become operational by
  Veterans Day, 2024.
  7) Within 24 hours after adoption of this Resolution, the Mayor shall
  transmit a letter notifying the Director of CalVet and other key State
  officials that the City Council has reaffirmed the City’s selection of the
  ARDA site, and is prepared to make the ARDA site available for
  development of the Southern California Veterans Memorial Park &
  Cemetery, in accordance with appropriate land acquisition and land
  transfer agreements.
